newsitem.title: JORDAN: PLO's Arafat urges world community to save peace.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Arafat urges world community to save peace.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on Tuesday urged the world to act to save the peace process, saying it was endangered by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's punitive actions.

"These (peace) accords are not bilateral, they are international, and I want to say now there is an international responsibility falling on all those who signed these accords to move to save the peace process from the crisis which Netanyahu is pushing it daily towards," Arafat told reporters in Amman.
The latest crisis in Palestinian-Israeli relations was
touched off by a twin suicide bombings in a Jewish market in Jerusalem last week in which 15 people were killed, including the two bombers, and 170 wounded.

Since the attack, Israel has imposed a closure on the West Bank and Gaza Strip, arrested 156 militants in areas under its control and threatened to enter Palestinian self-rule areas to fight militants if Arafat did not do the job.
Palestinians have said the Israeli measures are collective punishments that weaken Arafat and strengthen extremist forces.
"I am asking the international community to save and protect the peace process," Arafat said at the end of two days of talks with King Hussein and senior government officials in Amman.
The Palestinian leader praised both King Hussein and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak for their support to "get Israel to honour its commitments."
But Arafat criticised Washington for not shouldering its responsibility as a main sponsor of the peace process.

"Unfortunately the United States is not doing what it should do in its capacity as the main sponsor of the peace process in the Middle East," Arafat said ahead of an expected visit by U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross to the region to try to defuse the Israeli-Palestinian crisis.

Referring to the historic Washington ceremony in 1993 which sealed the peace accords, Arafat said:"I would like to remind that these accords were signed in the White House under the supervision of (U.S.) President Bill Clinton..."

Arafat said he had requested an urgent meeting of the U.N. Security Council because Israel was not only breaching its commitments under the peace accords but also violating human rights by its closure of Palestinian self-rule areas.

"I ask the world to move to stop this crime which the Israeli government is perpetrating against the Palestinian people...an air, land and sea siege, this is punishment against the Palestinian people as a whole," Arafat said.
Arafat described the closure as "criminal" measures aimed at humiliating Palestinians and imposing much human suffering while at the same wrecking the peace process.
"So clearly the objective and aim is to wreck the peace process and the objective and aim is to humilitiate the Palestinian people," Arafat added angrily.

Arafat also attacked Netanyahu personally, saying the Israeli leader was still a political novice. He also warned him of the consequences of his treatment of Palestinians, whom he described as a "people who will not be forced to their knees."

"I want to tell Netanhayu that he is still new to politics, he doesn't know the Palestinian people and also new to Israel because he spent most of his life outside, he doesn't know the Palestinian people or the Arab nation," Arafat said.
